pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

4. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

5. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

6. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

8. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

11. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.2.1 Study Skills: Note Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

7. A — went

8. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

9. A — Where is the library?

10. D — run

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 10.2.1 Study Skills: Note Making; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
